body:
## Problem and value

- Related issue: #1026 (bug report with reproductions and base measurements).
- Problem on the original base: at 360×760 the nav was a single scrolling row; `100%` and `Zoom in` were pushed outside the viewport, the route probe shared the nav's z-index and sat under it, and the presentation stage centred an oversized scene so its start edge could not be reached.
- Intended outcome: every nav action is reachable and hit-testable, every dock-owned overlay clears the bar, and the presentation stage can scroll across the whole scene.
- Worth maintaining: one measured dock height and five consumers, plus browser regression tests; no schema, renderer, or public contract change.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, and writing assistance.
- Tools/model: Hermes Agent (Nous Research), `deepseek-flash`; the agent reproduced the defects with CDP, edited the viewer sources, wrote the browser tests, ran the suites, and drafted this text. An independent three-seat review (Standards/Spec/Structure) ran on two cycles; blocking findings were fixed and re-reviewed. An earlier Claude audit found one stale generated proof artifact; it was rebuilt before this exact-head pass.
- Accountable contributor: @jahfaliabdulrahman-dev
- Problem origin: reproducible defects found during mobile inspection of a local Viewer build, then re-measured on the current base.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared Viewer behaviour (`viewer/viewer.css`, `viewer/viewer-chrome-layout.js`, `viewer/focus.js`, generated template).
- Coordinated slice: nav reachability, the measured dock clearance, and presentation start-edge reachability are one change. The cosmetic grouping of the three camera controls is explicitly deferred: they remain separate flex items and may wrap onto separate lines; no wrapper is introduced because it changed the toolbar's directional-key contract.
- `viewer-chrome-layout.js` publishes the measured dock height as `--archify-dock-h` (0 when hidden) before the desktop-only `eligible()` gate. This is intentionally separate from `--archify-nav-reserve`: the latter is the desktop stage-rail lift, while the former is the raw mobile dock height needed below that gate. The Passport fit reads that same measured dock and refits after placement; on the short-viewport compact path it moves below the dock when the space above is insufficient, using `--archify-passport-reserve` (the viewport-to-dock gap) for the CSS floor; the below-dock top is clamped inside the viewport. The regression guard covers the explaining position, the collapsed Passport at a mid-viewport dock, and a deep scroll past the dock. A schema-sized explanation scrolls inside the chip instead of growing through the dock.
- The stage, route probe, semantic lens, overview map and radar feedback consume the published band. The presentation stage uses `justify-content: flex-start` plus `margin-inline: auto` on the scene: fitting scenes stay centred and an oversized scene keeps its leading edge scrollable.
- Print: the print rule resets both `--archify-nav-reserve` and `--archify-dock-h` to `0px !important`. With scripts disabled, the mobile fallback would otherwise retain `6.25rem` of reserve: 116px of padding, 100px of it dead.
- Preserved: desktop stacking and layout, route-probe `data-route-dock="top"`, guide/finder visibility states, the wide-diagram scroll transform, dev's contrast tokens, parent navigation, short-viewport Passport handling, export notices, and the newer decoder diagnostics.

## Tests run

Base: `dev` @ `10b4dd5c`; head: **`c393fc7f`** (merge commit `4dfebf7e`, the compact Passport scroll clamp, the stronger collapsed/deep-scroll 320×300 guard, the full generated rebuild, and the README motion-proof refresh).

- `npm run test:generated` — pass at the final head.
- `test/viewer-mobile-chrome-browser.test.mjs` + `test/viewer-print-clearance-browser.test.mjs` + `test/passport-explanation-browser.test.mjs` + `test/semantic-legend-gateway.test.mjs` — **10/10 pass**.
- Browser regression set including `viewer-camera-browser.test.mjs` and `viewer-chrome-layout.test.mjs` — **50/50 pass**.
- `test/readme-showcase.test.mjs` — **14/14 pass** (one skipped) after rebuilding the motion proof from the final gallery artifacts.
- New focused test: 320×300, parent `meta.parentHref`, a schema-sized (≤1200 character) authored node explanation, `mobile: true`. It asserts the dock actually wraps (nav height > 1.5 button heights), every visible dock action stays inside the container and is hit-testable, `--archify-dock-h` covers the dock, the Passport title, prose and Back stay readable and clear of the dock (above it, or below it when the dock scrolls into the fixed chip) and the prose scrolls rather than being clipped, parent Back is hit-testable before the fixed Passport covers the header, and closing the explanation restores a hit-testable Explain focus. It asserts the reached `scrollY` for both offsets, so a short fixture cannot turn the mid/deep checks into clamped no-ops. It covers both the dock-flush position and a mid-viewport dock offset, so it is the guard for the merged composition, not a relabelled pre-integration capture.
- Shared boundary sample: rebuilt local `dev + #1001 + #1027` tree at the fixed #1027 head plus #1001 — `viewer-camera-browser.test.mjs`, `viewer-chrome-layout.test.mjs`, `viewer-mobile-chrome-browser.test.mjs` and `viewer-print-clearance-browser.test.mjs` — **44/44 pass**; the existing 175/225/300% camera assertions, dock/chrome checks and the new 320×300 sample all pass together.
- Not covered: no physical-device/printer run; the new sample is automated geometry/hit-test evidence, not a perceptual capture. Required CI at `c393fc7f` passed: https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40236775509. The separate FFmpeg 8.0 WebM decoder issue was tracked in #1061 and fixed by #1062, which is in `dev`; `webm-decode` also passes here.

## Visual evidence

- Existing mobile captures remain at their recorded earlier head; they are not relabelled as new-head evidence. No repeated Lens Clear/Copy or no-JS print captures are claimed.
- The new 320×300 check records geometry and hit-test results only; it does not claim a visual review of the composed screen.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify/assets/template.html` regenerated from the merged sources.
- 15 example pairs re-rendered; the five bundled drilldown pairs, `examples/ai-agent-n8n.html`, `docs/cases/mco-runtime.architecture.html` and `experiments/mco-showcase/mco-runtime.html` kept current; `docs/gallery.html` and its artifacts rebuilt; `examples/checkout-platform-delta.html` and receipt regenerated; `archify.zip` rebuilt (235 files).
- Dev's current `docs/assets/archify-live-proof.*` and export notices were retained; the proof was not refreshed merely because generated files were rebuilt.

## Attribution

The no-JS print reset and initial print regression were identified and prototyped by @BlueboxC in the fork correction at `28fbc157c608f985d0e4a2c6621230dcad12311b`; this PR adapts the authored one-line source change and regression test, preserving attribution in the test header and commit message. The fork commit also contains unrelated work and is not cherry-picked wholesale.

## Exact-head status

- Local generated and targeted checks above pass at `c393fc7f`; the same composition guard also passed a 360×760 recurrence with the long fixture during verification (the compact fix does not change the non-compact path).
- CI run 40236775509 at `c393fc7f` is **green**: scope, full-regression (1/2), browser-regression (1/2), test (18/20/22/24), webm-decode, webm-artifact, package smoke (ubuntu/macos/windows), Windows test portability (Node 22/24), website, zip-freshness and published-update-manifest all pass. CodeRabbit completed (including the scroll-offset nitpick, fixed in this head). The PR remains `BLOCKED` by the required reviewer decision, not by a check; do not merge until the maintainer review completes.
